l.i: Præsentemq; refert una vel herba Deum: Aut operis series auctorem tota recensèt, Qui facit & læto cuncta vigore fovet. Emicat ex ipsis divina potentia terris, Et levis est cespes qui probat esse Deum.

main_text.l: Et hoc loco in Ionæ historia, dicitur divinitùs factum, ut erosa àverme cucurbita aresceret.
4. Bestiarum quinetiam & herbarum ministerio Deus quandoq; utitur ad exercenda iudicia sua mala.
Ezech.14.15. Si bestiam malam transire fecero per terram, & orbauerit eam,& fuerit desolata absq; transeunte propter bestiam.

Huc facit narratio de leone, qui occidit Prophetam missum in Bethel ad Regem Iarobeamum: 1.Reg.13.24. Et illa de ursis narratio, qui lacerauerunt quadraginta duos pueros, qui contumelia affecerant Elizæum prophetam: 2.Reg.2.24.

page.notes: No marginal notes on this page. The page opens mid-stanza: the first line of the verse is a continuation from the previous page. Doubtful readings: the Greek word in paragraph 5 (θηριότητα) is marked [?] because the scan is small and the letters are not fully legible; "Elizæum" is read from a ligature and may be slightly different. Printed spellings such as "ministerio", "erofa" and "arefceret" are given with long s written as plain s, as the rules require, and "tranfeunte" etc. follow the same rule. The printed orthography "Eliæin" at a line end is read as "Eliæ in".
